title: P0: Add behavioral guardrails to AGENTS.md — Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers
description:
## Finding (from Agent Value Alignment audit)

AGENTS.md provides workflow instructions (wai → beads → openspec, TDD, session discipline) but **no behavioral guardrails**. An AI assistant working on this repo has no guidance on what it should/shouldn't do beyond the workflow.

### What's missing

- **Goal Sandwich**: The primary objective must appear verbatim at top AND bottom of the prompt (lost-in-the-middle countermeasure)
- **Prohibited behaviors (negations)**: 5 explicit "DON'T:" statements — e.g., DON'T make breaking changes without an openspec proposal, DON'T skip tests, DON'T refactor without test coverage
- **Escalation triggers**: The 7 named types — when to stop and ask (uncertainty, scope boundary, resource limit, anomaly detection, human review trigger, conflicting instructions, high stakes)
- **Minimal Footprint clause**: Resource/side-effect constraints for the assistant
- **Drift detection**: Self-check loop (ALIGNMENT check before major actions)

Your AGENTS.md follows the standard wai template. Missing: all Layer 3 patterns (Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers, Minimal Footprint, drift detection). Also: README has no value proposition at all — add one.

### What to do

1. Add a Goal Sandwich: objective statement in first 5 lines AND last 5 lines of the AGENTS.md prompt area
2. Add a "## Prohibited" section with 5+ explicit DON'T statements
3. Add a "## Stop and Ask" section with escalation triggers
4. Add a "## Minimal Footprint" clause
5. If eval tests exist, add a note about behavioral regression; if not, file a follow-up

### Priority rationale (P0)

Without behavioral guardrails, assistant behavior is unconstrained — the most common failure mode for AI-assisted development is scope creep and silent drift.

### References
- agent-value-alignment skill: references/layer-3-runtime-prompt.md
- Full audit report: genesis-ntg (genesis repo)

title: fix: lines_code and lines_comment always computed as 0 in engine.rs
description:
lines_code, lines_comment, and lines_blank in MetricValues are always 0. The count_lines() function in metrics.rs returns placeholder zeros rather than real values.

Approach: use tree-sitter AST node classification (not raw line scanning) to avoid ambiguity with multi-line strings and doc comments.
- Walk all nodes in the file's parse tree
- Lines containing at least one comment node and no non-comment, non-whitespace nodes → lines_comment
- Lines containing at least one named non-comment node → lines_code
- Remaining non-empty lines → lines_blank
- Count distinct line numbers across all matching nodes

Acceptance examples:
- A file with 3 // comment lines, 10 code lines, 2 blank lines → reports lines_comment=3, lines_code=10, lines_blank=2
- A line with both code and a trailing comment counts as lines_code, not lines_comment
- The sum lines_code + lines_comment + lines_blank must equal the file's total non-empty line count

title: fix: cognitive complexity overcounts chained logical operators due to sequence_id always None
description: metrics.rs:84-96 deduplicates boolean-operator branches via sequence_id, but engine.rs:346-351 always sets sequence_id: None on every Branch it creates. The dedup arm (LogicalAnd|LogicalOr, Some(id)) is dead code. Each 'and'/'or' in 'a and b and c' counts as a separate branch instead of once, overcounting cognitive complexity. Fix: in engine.rs, assign a shared sequence_id to all sibling and/or nodes in the same boolean-operator chain.

title: fix: file_lines_max threshold computed but never checked at file level
description: EffectiveThresholds includes file_lines_max but analyze_path() in main.rs never checks module.lines_total against it. Per-file line count violations never fire. Fix: check module.lines_total against thresholds.file_lines_max in analyze_path() and surface violations in FileReport.

title: fix: ABC metric is computed and serialized but never checked against any threshold
description:
abc metric (MetricValues.abc) is computed, stored, and serialized but never checked against any threshold — no push_limit_violation call exists for it.

Fix path: add enforcement.
1. Add abc_max: Option<u32> to AppThresholds in config.rs
2. Add it to EffectiveThresholds and populate in for_role()
3. Call push_limit_violation for 'abc' in build_unit_report() when unit.metrics.abc > abc_max
4. Add a test: a function with ABC > threshold must produce a LimitViolation finding

Acceptance: a file with a function that exceeds abc_max produces a 'abc' violation in the report output.

title: fix: exported-threshold violations (exported_cyclomatic_max etc.) never fire
description: EffectiveThresholds::for_role() computes exported_* thresholds for library-role files, but build_unit_report() in main.rs:414-461 never calls push_limit_violation() for them. Library files can never produce exported-threshold violations regardless of how high their exported metrics climb. Fix: add push_limit_violation calls for exported_* fields when unit.is_exported and the threshold is Some(x).

title: Clojure: extract parameter names so params/params_max are not dead
description:
## Finding

The `params` metric is always 0 for Clojure, so the `params_max = 4` threshold can never fire. Measured on equivalent code:

```clojure
(defn with-params [a b & rest] ...)   → params: 0
```
```python
def with_params(a, b, *rest): ...    → params: 3
```

Root cause: `pretender/src/metric_application/params.rs::param_name` maps a fixed set of node kinds — `identifier`, `typed_parameter`, `default_parameter`, `typed_default_parameter`, `parameter`, `self_parameter`/`self`, `list_splat_pattern`/`dictionary_splat_pattern`. Clojure's parameter vector is a `vec_lit` whose children are `sym_lit`, so no parameter is ever named.

## What to do

- Extend parameter extraction to Clojure's `sym_lit` parameters — keeping the mapping grammar-scoped so no other language's behaviour changes (the Rust `&self` case shows the precedent).
- Extract the parameters of each arity vector — one parameter per binding (filed proposal D2 / task 2.2). The *granularity* of destructured parameters is the one item the proposal declares unsupported (Non-Goals, task 4.4): follow the proposal's wording and pin the behaviour with a fixture assertion rather than deciding it here.
- A variadic parameter should count as one parameter (Python's `*rest` counts as one — check the Python precedent so the two agree).

## Notes

- Changes reported `params` → gated behind `pretender-1v8k.1`.
- Risk to check: `params` feeds `params_max`; making it non-zero may surface new violations in existing Clojure code — the baseline ledger may only shrink, never gain IDs.

## Spec delta

This ticket updates the deployed spec, not only the adapter:

- `openspec/specs/universal-code-model/spec.md` → **Requirement: Code Unit Model** (the parameter list of a code unit) and **Requirement: Tree-Sitter Query Contract**.

The change lands under `openspec/changes/` with a delta spec per requirement above; the
spec delta and the adapter change land in the same pull request.

## Red gate

`cargo test --test clojure_roundtrip_test` must fail before this change lands and pass after it.

- Before: a 3-parameter defn reports params: 0, so the asserted value 3 fails.
- After: the assertion holds.

## Anti-goals

- Do not weaken, relax or delete the fixture expectation to make the test pass.
- Do not change a threshold in `pretender.toml` to make the finding disappear.
- Do not change another language's reported metrics as a side effect.

## Regression suite (pass-to-pass)

- `cargo test --test clojure_roundtrip_test` — the other eight language round-trip targets stay green.
- `cargo test --lib` — engine, metric and plugin unit tests stay green.
- `just ci` — fmt, clippy, tests and the structural gate stay green.

## Ledger caveat

`pretender-baseline.json` may only **shrink** — never gain IDs. If this change surfaces new
findings in existing code, they are reported, not adopted into the ledger.

## Alignment with the filed proposal

Governed by `openspec/changes/close-python-clojure-fidelity/` (filed in `ee5abf6`, `openspec validate` clean): `proposal.md`,
`design.md` (decisions D1–D8), `tasks.md`, and the spec delta at
`openspec/changes/close-python-clojure-fidelity/specs/universal-code-model/spec.md`.

- This ticket implements proposal task(s): **2.2**.
- It must not decide anything the proposal already decided — where this ticket and the
  proposal disagree, the proposal wins and this ticket is updated.

## Co-modification note

file and rebase on any sibling that landed since — do not assume the state described in this

title: Clojure: capture multi-arity defn (functions are currently invisible)
description:
## Finding

Multi-arity `defn` is **not captured at all**. Measured:

```clojure
(defn multi-arity
  ([x] x)
  ([x y] (+ x y)))
```
→ absent from `pretender complexity` output and absent from `pretender check` units. The file contributes no units, so every per-unit threshold passes silently. A whole file of multi-arity functions analyzes as clean — the worst failure mode for a gate: *false green*.

Root cause: `pretender/languages/clojure/metrics.scm` matches `defn` only in the shape `(defn <name> <vec_lit> <body>)`. The multi-arity shape is `(defn <name> (<vec_lit> <body>) (<vec-lit> <body> ...))` — a list of arity lists, which no pattern matches.

## What to do

- Extend the query to match the multi-arity shape and emit one unit per arity.
- Decide, in the proposal, how the units are named (`multi-arity`, `multi-arity/2`?) and whether each arity counts separately for `function_lines` / `params` (the arities usually have different parameter lists — so `params` must come from the arity, not the `defn`).
- Add a fixture (`clojure_multi_arity_sample.clj`) and round-trip assertions.

## Notes

- Changes the reported unit set for existing Clojure code → gated behind `pretender-1v8k.1`.
- Related: the Clojure unit kind is always `Function` (no `Method`/`Ctor`); `defmulti`/`defmethod` and `deftype`/`defrecord`/`defprotocol` members are likewise invisible — same family of gap, tracked separately where the fix differs.

## Spec delta

This ticket updates the deployed spec, not only the adapter:

- `openspec/specs/universal-code-model/spec.md` → **Requirement: Tree-Sitter Query Contract** (the `defn` shapes the adapter must match) and **Requirement: Code Unit Model** (one code unit per arity, and its parameter list).

The change lands under `openspec/changes/` with a delta spec per requirement above; the
spec delta and the adapter change land in the same pull request.

title: File the openspec proposal for Python and Clojure capture coverage
description:
## Why this ticket first

Every child of `pretender-1v8k` that adds a capture, extracts a parameter, or re-models a branch **changes what the reported metrics are** for Python and/or Clojure. Project rule: *don't change a rule's outcome or default threshold without an openspec proposal*. This ticket is that proposal; the outcome-changing children are blocked by it.

## What the proposal must specify

1. **Capture set per language** — Python: `match_statement` / `case_clause`, comprehension clauses; Clojure: multi-arity `defn`, `deftest`, `is`-family assertions, per-clause `cond`/`case`, `recur`, nesting model.
2. **Weights** — cyclomatic/cognitive per new branch capture, and whether a new construct is a branch, a call, or neither (this is what decides the Clojure ABC fix: control forms must stop counting as calls).
3. **Metric deltas** — the expected before/after value of each affected metric on a named fixture, per language.
4. **Declared-unsupported list** — the metrics a language cannot support (Clojure type definitions, destructured parameters), written down in the language README so silence is intentional rather than accidental.
5. **Spec deltas** — scenario-level deltas under `openspec/specs/` for every affected requirement.

## Constraints

- Thresholds in `pretender.toml` stay untouched; this proposal changes *what is measured*, not *when a violation fires*.
- SARIF output stays schema-compatible.
- No new tree-sitter grammar: the pinned `tree-sitter-clojure` 0.1.0 and `tree-sitter-python` 0.25 grammars are the only inputs.

## Out of scope

The language-registry epic (`pretender-b5us`) — this proposal assumes the current per-language adapter shape and must not pre-empt that refactor.

## Red gate

Not applicable in the TDD sense — this ticket produces a proposal, not code. Its gate is
mechanical and runnable verbatim:

- `openspec validate <change-name> --strict` — must pass **for the new change only**.
  (The repo-wide `openspec validate --all --strict` reports 5 pre-existing failures
  unrelated to this work — see `pretender-2uv` — so it is not a usable gate here.)
- The change's `tasks.md` lists one task per child ticket in `pretender-1v8k`.

## Anti-goals

- No threshold change in `pretender.toml` — this proposal changes *what is measured*, not
  *when a violation fires*.
- No SARIF schema change.
- No new tree-sitter grammar: the pinned `tree-sitter-clojure` 0.1.0 and
  `tree-sitter-python` 0.25 grammars are the only inputs.
- Do not re-open the settled zero-type-capture decision (see the archived design D2/D3
  referenced below) without an explicit human decision.

## Traceability

- Archived design that settled Clojure's zero type captures:
  `openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-19-add-data-model-checks/design.md` (D2/D3) and its
  language coverage matrix.
acceptance_criteria: An openspec change exists with the capture set, the weights, the per-metric deltas and the declared-unsupported list; 'openspec validate <change-name> --strict' passes for the new change; spec deltas exist for every affected scenario; the change's task list names one task per outcome-changing child of pretender-1v8k.

title: Analyzer fidelity: close the measured metric gaps in the Python and Clojure adapters
description:
## Finding

Measured audit of the two adapters (fixtures + edge-case files, binary built from a clean HEAD worktree):

**Python — strong.** All function forms (top-level, method, nested, decorated, `async def`) are captured; cyclomatic matches hand-computed values; cognitive complexity and `nesting_max` are nesting-weighted correctly; `params` are extracted; `Method`/`Ctor` kinds resolve via `class_definition`; type definitions and annotated fields round-trip; `assert` / unittest / pytest assertions are counted; test-role detection works.

**Clojure — cyclomatic only.** `defn`/`defn-` detection and the branch set (`if/when/cond/case/loop/doseq/try/catch/and/or`) work, but a large part of the metric surface is flat or dead:

| Metric | Python | Clojure | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `params` | 3 | 0 | `params_max=4` never fires |
| `nesting_max` | 3 | 0 | `nesting_max=3` never fires; cognitive under-reports (3 vs 6 on identical code) |
| `assertions` | 2 | 0 | `min_assertions=1` is vacuous; `deftest` forms are not captured at all — a Clojure test file analyzes as **zero units** |
| `abc` | 1.73 | 4.12 | inflated: every list form (`if`, `let`) is counted as a call |
| multi-arity `defn` | n/a | **not captured** | the function is invisible → the file looks empty and passes every threshold silently |
| `cond`/`case` clauses | n/a | 1 branch per form | a 3-clause `cond` counts 1 (TS `switch` with 2 cases counts 3) |
| type definitions | Class + fields | none (by design) | data-model checks (primitive obsession, inheritance depth, mutable state) are silent for Clojure |
| unit kind | Function/Method/Ctor | Function only | no Method/Ctor |

**Python blind spots** (documented, but they under-report complexity): `match`/`case` arms contribute 0 branches (`match_case` → cyclomatic 1), and comprehension `if` filters contribute 0 (`comp` → cyclomatic 1).

## Scope

Adapter-level work only: captures, parameter extraction, branch modelling, manifests, tests, docs. **No rule outcome or threshold changes without an openspec proposal** — the proposal ticket is the first child and blocks every outcome-changing child.

## Success Criteria

For every metric in the table above, the Clojure adapter either produces a correct value or the language README declares it unsupported. Every child ticket is closed with a red→green→refactor cycle and its own acceptance criteria met.
## Audit recipe (re-runnable)

The numbers in the finding table come from a binary built from a clean `HEAD` worktree, not
from memory. Re-run them before trusting any number in a child ticket:

```bash
# 1. build an isolated binary (the working tree may carry other work in progress)
git worktree add /tmp/pt-head HEAD && cd /tmp/pt-head && cargo build

# 2. per-function complexity for a language (paths may be files or directories)
/tmp/pt-head/target/debug/pretender complexity <path> --human

# 3. full metric dump per unit (cyclomatic, cognitive, assertions, params, nesting_max, abc)
/tmp/pt-head/target/debug/pretender check <path> --json | \
  python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(u['name'], u['metrics']) for f in d['data']['files'] for u in f['units']]"

# 4. a Clojure/Python pair for the ABC comparison (identical code, two languages)
#    -> clojure abc 4.12 vs python abc 1.73
```

Fixtures used by the child tickets live in `pretender/tests/fixtures/`; the Clojure/Python
comparison pair is `pretender/tests/fixtures/clojure_sample.clj` and
`pretender/tests/fixtures/python_simple.py`.
acceptance_criteria: Every metric listed in the finding table either produces a correct value for Python and Clojure or is declared unsupported in the language README; all outcome-changing children are gated behind the openspec proposal ticket.

title: Governance gates suite (5 gates, one per child)
description:
## Why
Nothing currently prevents an agent from: adopting new debt into the baseline,
raising a threshold, widening `exclude`, disabling a rule for a role, or
deleting assertions. The epic's whole value depends on the gate being honest.

## Scope
Governance tests (next to `pretender/tests/repo_dogfood_test.rs`) asserting:
1. **Baseline monotonicity** — the committed baseline's ID set is a SUBSET of
   `origin/main`'s baseline. Additions are impossible. (Kills adopt-gaming,
   rename-gaming, and baselining new debt.)
2. **Baseline purity** — no baseline ID matches `pretender/src/` or
   `pretender/tests/` (the ratchet's proof).
3. **Threshold floor** — a committed floor file records the maximum allowed
   value per threshold key; current `pretender.toml` values must be <= the
   floor, and the floor file must only ever tighten (git history is the audit
   trail). Covers role tables (`[thresholds.test]`, `[thresholds.library]`,
   `[thresholds.script]`) so `x = 0` cannot disable a rule.
4. **Exclude allowlist** — `exclude` equals exactly the four known patterns.
5. **Assertion non-regression** — the total `assertions` metric across the
   repo must not decrease (pretender already measures it per unit).

## Acceptance
- Each gate has a test that FAILS when the corresponding gaming move is made
  (demonstrate: add a baseline ID -> test fails; raise a threshold -> fails).
- The tests pass on the current tree.
- `just ci` includes them.
acceptance_criteria: Every gate (.19.1-.19.5) has a test that fails when its gaming move is performed; all five are wired into `just ci`.

title: Language registry: replace dispatch branches with declarative per-language records (OCP + cohesion)
description:
## Why
The clearest open-closed violation in the codebase is language dispatch.
`pretender/src/engine.rs::parse` is `cyclomatic 26 / cognitive 89 / abc 99 /
188 lines` — a branch tree that must grow every time a language is added.
Meanwhile each language module repeats the same shape: `manifest` / `engine` /
`parse` (c.rs, go.rs, java.rs, javascript.rs, python.rs, ruby.rs, rust.rs,
typescript.rs, plus c/cpp/csharp/clojure/julia/r). The result is duplication
*and* a design that punishes the next language.

## Desired end state
Adding a language = adding a **record** (data), not editing a `match`. Each
language module owns its own queries and its own types (cohesion), and the
analyzer dispatches through a declarative registry (open/closed). The registry
is the natural home for the already-documented plugin surface
(`pretender plugins` — "not yet implemented").

## Scope
- Research the current dispatch surface and the plugin contract.
- Design the registry shape (trait-based adapters vs data records) and the
  migration path that keeps every language working at every step.
- Migrate language by language, deleting the old dispatch at the end.
- No rule outcomes, thresholds, CLI behavior, or SARIF schema change.

## Out of scope
- The mechanical file-splitting work of epic pretender-5zo (this epic depends
  on it being *planned*, not on it being finished).
- Changing what any rule measures.

## Acceptance
- `pretender/src/engine.rs::parse` complexity is within the epic's target
  thresholds (cyclomatic ≤ 5, cognitive ≤ 8).
- Adding a language requires no edit to the analyzer core (demonstrated by a
  test that registers a fake language).
- No duplicated `manifest/engine/parse` shape left across language modules.
- All existing tests pass unchanged (pass-to-pass).

## Notes
This epic is separate from pretender-5zo on purpose: pretender-5zo is a purely
tidy-first refactor epic (no design changes), this one is a design change and
needs its own research → design → proposal → implementation cycle.
acceptance_criteria: A new language is added by registering a record, not by editing the analyzer core; engine.rs::parse is within the target thresholds; `cargo test` green.
close_reason: Epic complete: research + design + migration steps 1-6 (PRs #70, #71) + measurement. Adding a language = one LangRecord + one Grammar arm + data files; zero dispatch-site edits (collect and mutation derive extension sets from REGISTRY). Byte-identity green at every commit; independent reviews passed on both PRs; all children closed.

title: Dogfood: run pretender's structural gate in CI (just ci → just dogfood)

## Problem
The structural gate existed only as a local lefthook pre-commit hook. CI ran

## Scope

- `pretender.toml`: `mode = "gate"` (single source of truth for the mode) and
  `exclude` gains `**/fixtures/**` — fixtures are deliberate counterexamples,
  not production code.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: comment documenting that `just ci` gates.
- `pretender/tests/repo_dogfood_test.rs`: governance test that pins the wiring

- `just ci` green; gate reports `164 known (baselined), 0 new`.

title: Make pretender's own code easy to understand: tighten structural thresholds via tidy-first refactors
description:
## Goal
End state: pretender's own source is simple enough that the gate *proves* it —
every function and file inside tight thresholds, enforced by CI, with a baseline
containing no production-code findings.

Today the gate is green only because `pretender-baseline.json` grandfathers 164
findings in `pretender/src` + `pretender/tests` (27 files).

## Target thresholds (end state, locked in by .15)
cyclomatic <= 5, cognitive <= 8, function_lines <= 20, file_lines <= 300,
nesting <= 2, abc <= 20, unwraps 0 in app code, duplication <= 3%.

## Ticket shape: vertical slices, one module per PR
The epic is decomposed **per module**, not per rule: a slice takes one module and
makes it clean across every rule in one PR. Rule sweeps across many files were
removed (resliced on 2026-11-24: horizontal tickets .6-.14 are closed and
superseded). The phase list below is a *metric dashboard*, not a work order.

## Ticket groups
- **Control surface** — .18 contract + template, .19 (container) with .19.1-.19.5
  (one mechanical gate each), .20 golden behavior corpus, .21 `just dogfood-red`,
  .22 independence wiring, .15 the ratchet.
- **Decomposition containers** (not schedulable; children are the work):
  .2 main.rs (.2.1-.2.5), .3 engine.rs (.3.1-.3.4), .4 cli_test.rs (.4.1-.4.4),
  .5 the remaining >400-line files (.5.1-.5.6).
- **Vertical slices** — .23 coupling.rs, .24 model.rs, .25 primitive_obsession.rs,
  .26 doctor.rs, .27 duplication.rs, .28 javascript.rs, .29 mutability_metrics.rs,
  .30 typescript.rs, .31 data_model.rs, .32 external_plugin.rs,
  .33 mock_detector.rs, .34 genesis_compile_test.rs, .35 cluster_detector.rs,
  .36 cpp.rs, .37 csharp.rs, .38 java.rs, .39 julia.rs, .40 python.rs.
- **Phase-0 trust** — pretender-6tt (Rust `params` never captured: params_max is
  unenforced on our own code; needs an openspec proposal first), pretender-gv5
  (void_mutator flapping: CI flake risk now that the gate is in CI). Both block
  every refactor slice.
- **Stragglers** — .16 CONTRIBUTING docs, .17 pre-commit hook must use the
  checkout's build.

## THE LEDGER MODEL (binding)
The baseline IS the burn-down ledger: it lists the findings still grandfathered.
1. RED — remove the ticket's finding IDs from `pretender-baseline.json`
   (un-grandfather). `just dogfood` then FAILS with exactly those findings.
2. GREEN — refactor until the gate passes.
3. TIDY — renames and dead-code removal in a separate commit.
4. NO ADOPTIONS. The baseline may only shrink; additions are mechanically
   impossible (monotonicity gate, .19.1). `--adopt` is forbidden in this epic.
5. RATCHET — only when a whole rule class is clean repo-wide: tighten that one
   threshold, then re-adopt once, deliberately, in .15.

## The ticket contract (binding; published in .18)
research (why this seam, with evidence) -> design (module responsibility map +
extraction plan) -> RED (un-grandfather; the gate fails) -> GREEN (refactor, no
behavior change) -> TIDY (separate commit) -> independent review (different
agent; /ro5 or parallel-review wave; verdict committed as a wai review artifact)
-> mechanical gates green -> ledger updated.
Per ticket: `wai pipeline start tdd-ro5u --topic="<ticket>"` — the pipeline runs at
TICKET level.

## Independence (binding; wired in .22)
Implementer bead and reviewer bead have different assignees; the implementer's
bead carries a bead gate awaiting the reviewer's bead; a gh:pr gate requires the
PR to be merged; disagreement escalates to a human gate.

## Mechanical gates (all in CI)
1. the structural gate (`just dogfood`);
2. baseline monotonicity (.19.1);
3. baseline purity (.19.2);
4. threshold floor, incl. role tables (.19.3);
5. exclude allowlist (.19.4);
6. assertion non-regression (.19.5);
7. golden behavior (.20);
8. independent review (.22).

## Rules of the epic
- Pure refactor only: no behavior change, no new features, no change to the
  tool's rule defaults (that needs an openspec proposal), no CLI/SARIF change.
- Tidy First: RED -> GREEN -> TIDY.
- One module per PR; PR under 400 changed lines; a slice that does not fit one
  session is split again, never scaled up.
- Thresholds only move in the tightening direction, and only in .15.
- Anti-gaming: no threshold raising, no exclude widening, no rule disabling, no
  assertion deletion, no code moved out of the scanned scope. Each is blocked by a
  mechanical gate.
- Every created or reshaped source file carries a Purpose/Responsibilities/
  Rationale header.

## Related epic
The language-dispatch redesign (declarative per-language registry — the
codebase's real open/closed violation) is filed separately as **pretender-b5us**,
with its own research -> design -> proposal -> implementation cycle. Its
research ticket informs the engine.rs split (.3): the split must not freeze the
dispatch shape.

## Definition of done
- `just ci` passes with the tightened thresholds and a baseline containing no
  production-code findings.
- `pretender check .` reports 0 violations in `pretender/src` and
  `pretender/tests` at the target thresholds.
- Every ticket went through the contract with an independent review.
- CONTRIBUTING documents the standard and the ledger workflow.

title: pretender init overwrites wai/dont-owned AGENTS.md regions and then calls them drifted
description:
Found while removing the retired OPENSPEC block (cf49a70). managed_block_specs() still injects WAI and DONT blocks authored by pretender.

Call path: InitArgs::run -> inject_managed_blocks (main.rs) -> BlockInjector::with_provenance("pretender").inject(AGENTS.md, "WAI"|"DONT", ...). genesis 0.12.3 inject replaces everything between a found marker pair, so a genuine wai- or dont-authored block is destroyed and replaced by pretender's one-line body with a pretender provenance footer. doctor.rs drift_targets() regenerates the same content, so pretender then reports the real tool's block as drifted and recommends 'pretender init' as the fix — a destructive loop.

Fix options: own no suite-foreign region (drop WAI/DONT like OPENSPEC), or inject only when the block is absent and carries no foreign provenance footer, and drop the matching doctor drift targets.

Meter: in a repo with a wai-authored WAI block, 'pretender init' leaves the block byte-identical; 'pretender check' reports no drift for it.
close_reason: Fixed: pretender owns no AGENTS.md region. managed_block_specs/inject_managed_blocks and the doctor's ManagedBlockDrift target are gone; init performs no block writes and the supported set is empty (pinned by a test). CLI test seeds wai/dont-authored blocks, runs init, asserts byte-identical file and no drift finding in check or doctor. adopt-genesis delta states the ownership rule; changelog records it. just ci green; pretender check --mode gate 0 new; pushed.

title: min_assertions miscounts assertions in Rust and Julia test functions
description: Evidence: pretender's own .pretender/history shows 236/289 events are min_assertions reds, nearly every test in pretender/tests/cli_test.rs flagged with assertions=0 despite using assert!/assert_eq!. Same dominates wai (1435/1898) and testaruda (3798/8817) histories. Root cause hypothesis: tree-sitter extraction counts only literal assert-style call expressions and misses Rust assertion macros (assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert*, panic!/unreachable!/todo! in tests, Result-returning #[test] fn with ?) and Julia @test/@test_throws/@test_broken macros in @testset blocks. Consequence: false reds dominate the advisory channel, agents learn to ignore findings (0 in-session edits after violations across all repos in pi session history) — this noise is the prerequisite blocker for the agents-act-on-findings loop. Investigate: (1) confirm which assertion forms the extractor currently recognizes per language; (2) enumerate missing forms for Rust and Julia from tree-sitter grammars; (3) fix counting with red->green tests per form (TDD, one failing test per missing assertion form). Acceptance: cli_test.rs functions with assert_eq! report assertions>0; Julia @test functions report >0; no regression in python/rust/js existing counts; events.jsonl on a full pretender self-scan shows min_assertions events drop by >80% vs current 236.
close_reason: Merged via PR #16 (squash, 6f4d229). Rust/Julia assertion macros now counted; 0 false reds on genuine tests; self-scan min_assertions 236->134. Remaining fixture/helper scope question tracked in pretender-68j.

title: fix: get_parser() builds dead registry and is called per-file inside par_iter()
description:
Two related defects in get_parser() / main.rs that should be fixed together:

1. Dead registry (main.rs:539-558): get_parser() constructs a ParserRegistry, queries it, discards the result (_p), then runs a second parallel match on the extension. The registry result is never used.

2. Per-file rebuilding (main.rs:282-286): get_parser() is called inside par_iter(), so a new ParserRegistry is constructed for every file analyzed in parallel. Registry construction is O(n) repeated work.

Fix: remove ParserRegistry from get_parser() entirely. Build the registry once in run() and resolve the parser before entering par_iter(). Pass the resolved parser (or language) into analyze_path() directly. This eliminates both the dead work and the repeated allocation.

Acceptance:
- ParserRegistry is constructed exactly once per invocation
- get_parser() no longer references ParserRegistry
- analyze_path() receives the resolved parser, not a file extension
- Existing analysis output is unchanged

title: Clojure: per-clause cond/case, recur as a branch, no double-counted try/catch
description:
## Finding

Three branch-modelling defects in the Clojure adapter, all measured:

1. **`cond`/`case` clauses collapse.** A 3-clause `cond` counts as **one** branch (`condy: 2` = base + 1). The TypeScript adapter counts each `case` (a 2-case `switch` → 3), so Clojure under-reports the classic multi-way branch.
2. **`recur` counts zero.** `recur` is a loop back-edge — a real control-flow decision — but the branch set is `^(loop|for|doseq)$`, so a `loop`/`recur` pair contributes 1 (the `loop` only). Measured: `updater` → 3 (base + `loop` + `if`).
3. **`try` and `catch` both count.** `(try … (catch …))` adds **2** (measured `catcher: 3` = base + try + catch) although it is one error-handling construct — and `catch` alone (without `try`) also counts, which double-counts the same construct from two directions.

## What to do

- Capture `cond`/`case` per clause (mirror the `branch.switch_case` kind the TypeScript adapter uses), so a 3-clause `cond` counts 3.
- Count `try` **or** `catch`, not both; a `catch` outside a `try` must not add a second count.
- Decide the treatment of `recur`: as a loop branch (weight 1/1) or as a loop terminator that carries no extra weight — settle it in the proposal, once, and apply it to `loop`/`recur` together.

## Notes

- Changes reported cyclomatic/cognitive → governed by the filed proposal `openspec/changes/close-python-clojure-fidelity/` (parent `pretender-1v8k.1`, closed in `cdf1138`).

## Closed as merged

Folded into `pretender-1v8k.9` (review finding SCOPE-001): branch granularity and
call/branch separation are one decision about the Clojure capture boundary, and both
halves rewrote the same query file. The merged ticket carries both acceptance sets.
acceptance_criteria: A 3-clause cond counts 3 branches, a loop/recur pair follows the agreed rule, and a try with one catch counts exactly one error-handling branch; fixture expectations are asserted in the round-trip test.

title: Clojure: rework the capture boundary — control forms are not calls, branches count per clause
description:
## Finding (merged scope: branch granularity + call/branch separation)

The ABC metric is inflated for Clojure because **every list form counts as a call**. Measured on identical code:

```clojure
(defn g [a]
  (if (pos? a)
    (let [b (inc a)]
      (println b))))          → abc 4.12
```
```python
def g(a):
    if a > 0:
        b = a + 1
        print(b)               → abc 1.73
```

The `if` and `let` forms are counted as call sites (`@call` matches *any* `list_lit` whose first child is a symbol), so C-count is inflated by every control form. Since `abc_max = 30` is a real threshold, Clojure files are systematically closer to the limit than equivalent Python files.

Root cause: `pretender/languages/clojure/metrics.scm` has `(list_lit value: (sym_lit) @call.callee) @call` with no exclusion of special forms.

## What to do

- Take the control forms out of the C-count by **capture precedence**, not by a blocklist (filed proposal D3): the branch/assignment/definition/assertion captures consume a form first, and `@call` matches only unconsumed leading-`sym_lit` list forms. A blocklist rots with every new branch kind; precedence is structural.
- `try` and `finally` no longer branch; one `@branch.catch` per catch clause (filed proposal task 1.2).
- `cond`/`case`/`condp` contribute one branch per test/result pair; the dispatch expression is not a branch (filed proposal D7).
- `recur` is its own branch kind, `@branch.recur` (filed proposal task 2.3).
- ABC stays a structural metric at 1.0 per call — the `[smell_weights]` values feed smell detection, not the C-count (filed proposal D6, option (a)). Pin that reading with a unit test.

title: Clojure: model nesting so nesting_max and cognitive complexity are not flat
description:
## Finding

`nesting_max` is always 0 for Clojure and cognitive complexity ignores nesting. Measured on equivalent nested code:

title: Baseline hygiene: just dogfood-adopt + the refactor-PR baseline agreement
description:
## Problem
Finding IDs are `file::symbol::rule` (function rules) and `file::::rule` (file

function therefore needs a baseline refresh, and the refresh must be reviewable.

## Scope
- Add a `just dogfood-adopt` recipe: run the gate in adopt mode and print the
  baseline diff (`git diff --stat pretender-baseline.json` + the changed IDs).
- Document the working agreement: a refactor PR ships the refreshed baseline; the
  reviewer checks the diff contains only renames/moves, never a new rule on new
  code.
- Add a short note in CONTRIBUTING.

## Acceptance
- `just dogfood-adopt` exists and shows the ID-level diff.
- `just ci` still green.
- No threshold or rule behaviour changed.
notes: SUPERSEDED by the baseline-as-ledger model (RO5U review 2026-11-24). The original idea — 'just dogfood-adopt' refreshes the baseline on every refactor PR — is now FORBIDDEN: adopt-gaming is the main way an agent could hide new debt. The replacement model: the baseline IS the burn-down ledger; a ticket REMOVES its finding IDs (un-grandfather) to get a real RED, and the refactor makes the gate green again. Baseline additions are impossible (enforced by the monotonicity gate in pretender-5zo.19). Mechanisation: pretender-5zo.21 (just dogfood-red).
close_reason: Superseded by the baseline-as-ledger model: the baseline becomes a monotonically shrinking burn-down ledger (RED = un-grandfather the finding), additions are forbidden. Replaced by pretender-5zo.19 (monotonicity gate) and pretender-5zo.21 (just dogfood-red).

title: Terminate hanging or noisy external scanners within configured budgets
description:
## Parent
Security evaluation 2026-10-09, SEC-02; parent workspace charly/reports/security-2026-10-09.md (report commit 2a09a4c). Evidence below is self-contained for this repository.

## What to build
Terminate hanging or noisy external scanners within configured budgets. This slice delivers one observable protection from input through execution/storage to user-facing diagnostics.

**Evidence / baseline:** External scanner output() has no timeout or captured-output bound.

**Lane:** DESIGN. **Complexity:** L.
Design/security invariants must be settled before implementation; use OpenSpec where required by the repository. This ticket authorizes remediation planning, not an unreviewed protocol break.

**Files / Systems:**
- `pretender/src/external_plugin.rs`
- `pretender/src/config.rs`

**Baseline:** External scanner output() has no timeout or captured-output bound.
**Regression suite:** cargo test --locked

- [ ] Set numeric timeout and output-byte limits and include the applicable limit in errors.

Feedback from specodelic (downstream consumer, pretender 0.7.0):

Every repo embedding pretender as a gate must hand-maintain an exclude list for generated/vendored/scratch dirs. specodelic's pretender.toml carries: `target/**`, `./target/**`, `book/**`, `./book/**`, `docs/**`, `./docs/**`, `vendor/**`, `./vendor/**`, `node_modules/**`, `./node_modules/**`, `**/*_generated.*` — and the ./-prefixed twins exist only because walked paths are ./-anchored (specodelic commit d864425, and its own d2fca7a addendum missed the ./vendor/** variant until 2026-10-09, leaking 104 vendored-mermaid findings into the walk gate).

Proposal: when walking (collect_input_files / collect_path), default-filter any directory that is git-ignored (resolve via the repo's .gitignore + global/core.excludesFile, e.g. the `ignore` crate). Config exclude remains the override for cases where users WANT to scan ignored files (add an opt-out flag like `--scan-ignored` or config `pretender.respect_gitignore = false`, default true).

Benefits:
- zero-config correctness: target/, node_modules/, vendored minified JS stop being scanned without each repo enumerating them
- kills the ./-anchoring footgun class entirely (patterns silently not matching ./-prefixed walked paths)
- consistent with how ripgrep/typos/etc. behave, so the mental model matches

Edge cases to design for:
- files matched but explicitly passed as PATHS args should still be scanned loudly (mirrors current 'explicitly passed paths keep the loud get_parser error' behavior)
- repos without git (no .gitignore): fall back to current behavior
- --staged path unaffected (git classifies staged files anyway; consumer vendor role blocks rely on that)
- --diff-only: intersection with gitignore filter is natural (both derive from git)

Acceptance criteria:
- In a repo where target/ and vendor/ are gitignored, `pretender check` does not scan them without any exclude config
- Explicit `pretender check vendor/` still scans and errors loudly on unsupported files
- A config/flag opt-out restores current exhaustive behavior
- Documented in README/config docs

## Why
cositos has an R backend that pretender cannot parse. `pretender check r/` returns `{"files":[]}` with exit 0. R is the dominant language for statistical computing and is widely used in data-science adjacent projects.

## Crate
`tree-sitter-r = "1.3.0"` is available on crates.io. Note: this is on a 1.x version line (not 0.23); check API compatibility with the current tree-sitter 0.23 integration layer before pinning.

## What to build
Following the exact pattern of existing language plugins:

1. Add `tree-sitter-r` to `pretender/Cargo.toml` (verify 0.23 API compat; pin to a compatible version).
2. Create `languages/r/plugin.toml` — extensions `[".r", ".R"]`, tree_sitter source, branch/assertion/smell_weights tables.
3. Create `languages/r/metrics.scm` — tree-sitter queries capturing:
   - Function definitions: `function_definition` (R uses `name <- function(...) {...}` — the name is typically an assignment LHS, not part of the function node; capture `function_definition` and walk up to the enclosing assignment for the name)
   - Branches: `if_statement`, `for_statement`, `while_statement`, `tryCatch` call detection
   - Calls and assignments for ABC metric
4. Register the plugin in the builtin registry.
5. Add a test fixture `tests/fixtures/r/` with a sample `.R` file and a detection test.

## Note on R grammar complexity
R's grammar is unusual: functions are anonymous by default and typically assigned. The `metrics.scm` may need to handle the `left_assignment` / `right_assignment` node wrapping a `function_definition`. Review how tree-sitter-r models this before writing queries.

## Acceptance
`pretender check tests/fixtures/r/` parses at least one function, reports metrics, and exits 0.

title: [bug] F19: pretender exits 0 with empty results on paths containing no supported-language files
description:
## Finding
From cositos dogfooding evaluation (sandbox/charly-vibes-tools/dev-tooling-evaluation.md §F19).

`pretender check <path>` exits 0 and returns `{"files":[]}` when given a directory containing only unsupported languages (e.g. Julia, C#, R, Clojure). No warning, no error, just silent empty success.

## Reproduction
```
# cositos project added Julia, C#, R, Clojure backends after initial Python+JS setup
pretender check julia/src csharp r clojure/src
→ {"files": []}   # exit 0
```

## Impact
The complexity gate appears comprehensive (it runs, exits 0) but it only covers the original languages. Every new backend added in a language pretender can't parse is silently unchecked forever. This gives *false confidence* — the gate looks green but it only covers a fraction of the codebase.

In cositos this was worked around with a manual coverage-manifest gate (a checked-in file listing every backend directory with its declared quality-tool binding; a build step fails if a directory is undeclared or claims pretender coverage but pretender parses zero files). But the root fix belongs in pretender.

## Supported languages (for reference)
C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Ruby, Rust, TypeScript.

## Suggested fix
When explicit paths are supplied and zero files match any supported grammar, exit non-zero (or at minimum emit a loud warning to stderr) with a message like:
```
warning: no files matched a supported grammar in: julia/src, csharp, r, clojure/src
```
This turns "silently uncovered" into a caught misconfiguration.
acceptance_criteria:
`pretender check <dir>` exits non-zero (or emits a stderr warning) when the given paths produce zero parsed files and no supported language grammar matched.
`pretender check <supported-lang-dir>` (e.g. a Python or JS tree) is unaffected.
A test fixture in `tests/` covers the empty-result path (a directory containing only an unsupported-language file) and asserts the non-zero exit or warning output.
notes: Likely change site: the file-walker / grammar-dispatch logic in pretender check (src/check.rs or equivalent). The guard should only fire when explicit paths are supplied and zero files match — not when a path simply happens to have no violations.

title: check shows ✗ in guidance/tiered mode even though it exits 0
description:
In `guidance` and `tiered` modes, `pretender check` exits with code 0 (success) even when violations exist, but the human output still marks files with ✗ and says VIOLATION. The visual signal contradicts the exit code semantics.

Fix: use mode-aware indicators in the human output:
- `guidance` → ⚠ advisory (exits 0)
- `tiered` → ⚠ advisory (exits 0)
- `gate` → ✗ blocking (exits 1 on violations)

Only gate mode should use ✗ and the word VIOLATION. Guidance and tiered should use ⚠ and say ADVISORY.

Verify: `pretender check pretender/src/config.rs --mode guidance` shows ⚠ and exits 0. `pretender check pretender/src/config.rs --mode gate` shows ✗ and exits 1.

title: complexity output shows raw scores with no threshold context

Users can't tell if 11 is a problem without separately running `pretender explain cyclomatic`. The output should include the configured threshold, similar to how `check` shows 'VIOLATION cyclomatic 11 > 10'.

title: Explore feedback loop: track recurring structural violations to surface as constraints
description:
When pretender catches structural violations (complexity, duplication, nesting depth), nothing persists this signal beyond the current session. This ticket explores how to track recurring violations and feed them back into the development process.

**Note:** pretender currently calculates metrics (cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity, nesting, ABC) but does not yet compare them against thresholds to emit violations. This ticket covers both: (1) designing the violation emission path, and (2) persisting and aggregating those signals.

## Deliverable

A design document at `pretender/docs/feedback-loop-design.md` answering the questions below, reviewed and approved. Followed by an implementation ticket.

## Starting points

- `pretender/src/config.rs:166-260` — threshold definitions (AppThresholds, TestThresholds, etc.)
- `pretender/src/metrics.rs:6-45` — metric calculations (cyclomatic, cognitive, nesting, ABC)
- `pretender/src/main.rs:44-73` — main entry: calculates metrics but doesn't compare to thresholds
- `pretender/src/roles.rs:171-231` — EffectiveThresholds applied per role

## Questions to answer

- What violation taxonomy to use? (pretender's existing threshold categories vs. something richer)
- How to aggregate: per project, per agent model, per code area?
- Should recurring violations auto-generate openspec constraints or pretender profile defaults?
- What threshold: how many occurrences before a pattern is "recurring"?

## Integration points

- openspec specs: surface recurring patterns as constraints in future proposals
- pretender profiles: auto-adjust thresholds based on project-specific violation history
- Agent prompts: inject "known weak spots" into system prompts for specific projects

## Sequencing

This is a generalization ticket. Start after the espectacular tracer-bullet proves the end-to-end feedback loop with one concrete signal.

## Finding

Each adapter's language README documents *what is tracked* but not **what is not measured**, and it never separates the two reasons a metric can be missing:

Without that distinction a reader cannot tell whether a missing Clojure metric is a known gap (a ticket exists) or a permanent limitation (no ticket will ever exist). Silence reads as "supported and clean".

## What to do

title: Clojure: complete the plugin.toml branch-weight table and guard it with a test
description:
## Finding

`pretender/languages/clojure/plugin.toml` declares branch weights for only three captures — `@branch.if`, `@branch.logical.and`, `@branch.logical.or` — while `metrics.scm` captures five: it also captures `@branch.loop` and `@branch.catch`.

The two undeclared captures work only because `metric_application::branch_spec` falls back to a 1/1 default. The manifest is therefore *not* a complete description of the adapter's branch semantics, and a future change to the default weight would silently move Clojure's metrics with no manifest diff to show for it.

The same drift is worth checking across adapters: the manifest is the place where branch semantics are supposed to be explicit.

## What to do

- Add the missing `@branch.loop` and `@branch.catch` entries to the Clojure manifest with the same 1/1 weights the other branch captures use.
- Add a consistency check (test) that every `@branch.*` capture in an adapter's `metrics.scm` has a corresponding manifest entry — so the gap cannot reappear in any language.
- The check must fail loudly on a missing entry rather than silently defaulting, otherwise it documents the drift instead of preventing it.

## Notes

- No metric outcome change (the weights are already 1/1 by default) → not gated behind `pretender-1v8k.1`.
## Red gate

`cargo test --lib plugin` must fail before this change lands and pass after it.

- Before: the clojure manifest is missing the @branch.loop and @branch.catch entries, so the consistency test fails
- After: the assertion holds.


## Anti-goals

- Do not make the consistency test pass by defaulting the missing weight silently — the
  point is to fail loudly and name the adapter and the capture.
- Do not change any adapter's measured metric as a side effect of adding the explicit
  1/1 entries (the default already is 1/1, so the numbers must not move).

## Regression suite (pass-to-pass)

- `cargo test --lib plugin` — the manifest unit tests stay green.
- `cargo test --test <lang>_roundtrip_test` — the other eight language round-trip targets stay green.
- `just ci` — fmt, clippy, tests and the structural gate stay green.

[bug] false 'Parse errors detected' warning: local named 'raw' referenced as &raw collides with &raw const/mut expression in tree-sitter-rust 0.23.3
description:
## Symptom

`pretender check` emits `"Warning": Parse errors detected in <file>` for Rust files that are perfectly valid Rust and parse cleanly with newer grammars. Metrics still compute (parser recovers), but the warning is noise and erodes trust in the check.

## Root cause

Pinned `tree-sitter-rust = "0.23"` (0.23.3 in Cargo.lock). In that grammar, the identifier sequence `&raw <ident>` triggers the `&raw const/mut` expression lookahead, producing an ERROR node when what follows doesn't match (e.g. a plain borrow of a local named `raw`):

```rust
fn read_cache(path: &Path) -> Option<CacheEntry> {
    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;   // <- local named raw
    serde_json::from_str(&raw).ok()                  // <- '&raw' here => ERROR node at '&raw'
}
```

Verified with tree-sitter 0.25.10 + tree-sitter-rust 0.23.3 (py-tree-sitter): ERROR node reported at the `&raw` token. The same file parses with **zero** errors under tree-sitter-rust **0.24.2**.

## Real-world trigger

genesis-vibes src/update_check.rs, tests/update_check.rs, tests/evals_guidelines_docs.rs all tripped this (v0.10.0 release scan). Workaround applied genesis-side: renamed the locals (contents/body_text/raw_json) — but any consumer with a local named `raw` used as `&raw` will hit this, and `raw` is a common variable name.

## Suggested fix

Bump tree-sitter-rust 0.23.x -> 0.24.x (0.24.2 verified to parse the repro cleanly). Need to confirm LANGUAGE_VERSION/ABI compatibility with the pinned tree-sitter 0.25 runtime before upgrading — 0.24 grammars target ABI 15 which should be fine, but verify with `pretender doctor` + the repro below after the bump.

## Minimal repro

```rust
// repro.rs
fn f(x: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let raw = x.to_string();
    Some(serde_json::from_str::<String>(&raw).unwrap_or_default())
}
```

`pretender check repro.rs` -> "Parse errors detected" with tree-sitter-rust 0.23.3; clean with 0.24.x.
close_reason: PR #39 merged (CI green): tree-sitter-rust 0.23→0.24.2, ABI-compatible with tree-sitter 0.25 runtime — false 'Parse errors detected' on &raw locals gone, metrics no longer silently lost (engine early-return path). No .scm query migrations needed.

title: feat: add Clojure language plugin (tree-sitter-clojure)
description:
## Why
cositos has a Clojure backend that pretender cannot parse. `pretender check clojure/src` returns `{"files":[]}` with exit 0. Clojure's functional style means traditional cyclomatic complexity is less meaningful, but nesting depth, parameter count, and function length are still useful signals.

## Crate
`tree-sitter-clojure = "0.1.0"` is available on crates.io. Note: this is an early 0.x release; verify tree-sitter API compatibility before pinning.

## What to build
Following the existing plugin pattern:

1. Add `tree-sitter-clojure` to `pretender/Cargo.toml` (verify compat).
2. Create `languages/clojure/plugin.toml` — extensions `[".clj", ".cljs", ".cljc", ".edn"]`, tree_sitter source, branch/assertion/smell_weights tables.
3. Create `languages/clojure/metrics.scm` — queries capturing:
   - Function definitions: `defn`, `defn-`, `fn` forms (list nodes with `defn`/`fn` as first symbol)
   - Branches: `if`, `when`, `cond`, `case`, `try`/`catch` forms
   - Nesting depth is particularly valuable for Clojure (deeply nested `let`/threading macros are a common smell)
4. Register the plugin in the builtin registry.
5. Add a test fixture `tests/fixtures/clojure/` with a sample `.clj` file and a detection test.

## Note on Clojure grammar complexity
Clojure's homoiconic syntax means all forms are lists; tree-sitter-clojure represents them as `list_lit` nodes. Function definitions and branches are identified by the first element being a specific symbol. This is structurally different from the C-family grammars — the `.scm` queries will need to match on symbol text, not node type.

Priority lowered to P3 because Clojure has smaller practical overlap with the cositos workflow compared to Julia/C#/R, and the grammar integration is more complex.
